column3: The Hebrew says “in the morning,” without an explicit “next,” and specifically says they spent the night there; BSB has “camped.”
The Hebrew has singular “your place”; BSB has plural “your positions.”
The Hebrew says “know the way”; BSB has “see the way.” It describes their lack of prior travel as “yesterday or the day before.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Joshua, repeats “the people,” and uses separate verbs for lifting the ark and going; BSB begins with “he” and ends with “them.”
The Hebrew says “I will be with you”; BSB uses “I am with you.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the Jordan twice; BSB leaves the first occurrence implicit after “waters.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Joshua and uses collective singular names for all seven peoples; BSB says “He continued” and uses plurals.
The Hebrew repeats “one man” for the distribution among tribes; BSB has simply “one from each tribe.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “the soles of the feet,” repeats “the waters of the Jordan,” and calls the heap “one”; BSB condenses these details.
The Hebrew explicitly mentions leaving their tents and repeats “the people”; BSB says “broke camp” and uses “them.”
The Hebrew repeats “carrying the ark” with the priests and describes the feet as dipped at the edge of the water; BSB says “touched.”
The Hebrew explicitly says the waters rose as “one heap”; BSB describes them as backing up upstream.
